svg.text: Anticipy Pendant — Stupid-Simple Build Guide (Bambu Lab P2S)
CLIP THE HEADER PINS OFF THE BOARD (2 minutes, do this first)
Flush cutters: snip each gold pin flush with the board, both sides. Board must end up 5 mm thick.
Nothing fits with the pins on. This is the single most important step.
Need cutters? amazon.ca → search "flush cutters electronics"
PICK YOUR VERSION & PRINT IT (silver PETG, files in firmware/case/pendant_v2/stl/)
A Slim (200 mAh) — shell_200mah + back_200mah — print ≈ 55 min + 25 min
C Workhorse (500 mAh + storage + USB) — shell_500mah_storage_usb + back_500mah_storage — ≈ 1 h 30 + 35 min
E Clean face, zero holes (200 mAh + buzz) — shell_200mah_clean + back_200mah_haptic — ≈ 55 min + 25 min
Slicer settings: 0.12 mm layer · 4 walls · 40% infill · outer wall 60 mm/s · front face DOWN on the textured plate · tree supports (build plate only)
SOLDER 2 WIRES (that's the whole circuit)
RED: battery + → BAT+ pad on the back of the board
BLACK: battery − → BAT− pad. Tape the leads apart while you work. Check polarity with a multimeter before power-on.
Kapton tape over the pads when done. Charging is automatic through USB-C — the charger chip is already on the board.
PAD & PLACE
Stick 1 mm foam on both faces of the battery. Battery goes in first (bottom), board on top, USB-C facing the bottom edge.
Storage version: press the flash board into the pocket inside the back cover before closing.
CLOSE IT — press, then 2 screws
Press the back cover in (the lip aligns it), then drive one M1.4 screw into each side hole. They self-tap — no nuts, no glue.
It cannot pop open. To recharge version A/E: remove 2 screws, pop the back.
CHAIN
Thread a 2.5–3 mm stainless chain straight through the hole in the top of the body. No jump rings, no glued loops, nothing to break.
amazon.ca → "2.5mm stainless steel necklace chain 60cm"
Your printer: P2S speed facts
• Max toolhead speed: 600 mm/s (spec) — never used for real parts
• Bambu PETG default: ~200 mm/s outer wall — too fast, looks sloppy
• For a silver jewelry finish: outer wall 60 mm/s, inner 120 mm/s
• These parts are tiny — the printer is idling either way.
• 0.12 mm "Fine" layers ≈ 2× the time of 0.20 mm, worth it here
• Textured PEI plate, 255 °C nozzle, 70 °C bed, glue stick optional
Times in Step 2 are at these settings; Bambu Studio shows exact time when you slice.
Amazon.ca (search, top Prime result)
• "502025 lipo battery 200mah 3.7v" — small battery
• "M1.4 self tapping screws laptop" — case screws
• "W25Q128 spi flash module" — storage board (~$10)
• "10mm coin vibration motor 3v" — haptic buzz
• "28 awg silicone wire kit" + "1mm adhesive eva foam sheet"
• "kapton tape 10mm" + "2.5mm stainless steel necklace chain 60cm"
You already have: 500 mAh battery, board, solder, PETG.
Plan for the 27th
Tonight: print Version A (≈ 1 h 20 total). Drop your board + battery in WITHOUT soldering — just check the fit.
Fits? Solder the 2 wires, close it, wear it. Then print Version C for the real demo unit (≈ 2 h).
Doesn't fit? Tell me which part rubs and by how much — it's a one-number fix and a reprint.
Everything above is in the repo: firmware/case/pendant_v2/ (STLs, CAD source, README).
